verdict.rationale: Terraform is itself an official first-party CLI, documented at developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli. It has automation-friendly features an AI agent can drive: `-json` machine-readable output and streaming JSON UI messages, `-auto-approve` for non-interactive applies, saved plan files for preview-then-execute, and Unix-tool-friendly state commands. Community users confirm hands-on CLI use such as `terraform state mv`, `rm` and `import`. Missing for 10: no documented AI- or agent-specific guidance for the CLI itself, and no independent corroboration of agents driving it.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: For long-running commands such as `plan`, `apply`, `refresh`, and `test`, the `-json` flag outputs a stream of JSON UI messages.
You can pass the `-auto-approve` option to instruct Terraform to apply the plan without asking for confirmation.
The CLI usage and output of the state commands is structured to be friendly for Unix tools such as grep, awk, etc.
Workaround for refactoring: use 'terraform state mv'.
